predecessors.name: Qing dynasty
predecessors.text: the Qing empire's China proper, Manchuria, Inner Mongolia and Xinjiang; Outer Mongolia declared independence in 1911-12 and Tibet went its own way

successors.name: People's Republic of China
successors.text: the Republic of China's Cliopatria shape of 1949

ledger.x: 1912: the Republic of China is inaugurated at Nanjing.
1912: the Qing abdicate and the Republic takes the empire's China.
1912: the Kumul khanate becomes the Republic's vassal.
1912: the government moves from Nanjing to Beijing.
1912: the Republic holds Chamdo and western Kham, west of the Yangtze.
1916: Yuan Shikai turns the Republic into an empire.
1916: the Republic is restored.
14 July 1916: the three seceded provinces return.
1917: Sun Yat-sen sets up a rival government at Guangzhou.
1918: Lhasa takes back Chamdo and western Kham.
1919: Beijing abolishes Outer Mongolia's autonomy.
ledger.cpn: Great Mongol State (Bogd Khanate of Mongolia)

ledger.x: 1921: Ungern-Sternberg takes Urga and the Chinese garrison goes.
ledger.cpn: Great Mongol State (Bogd Khanate of Mongolia)

ledger.x: 1921: the rest of Outer Mongolia leaves Chinese rule.
ledger.cpn: Great Mongol State (Bogd Khanate of Mongolia)

ledger.x: 10 December 1922: Japan returns Tsingtao.
1926: Guangxi's army joins the Northern Expedition: 'the NRA Seventh Army under Li Zongren'.
1926: Hunan falls to the Northern Expedition.
1926: Hubei falls.
1926: Jiangxi falls.
1926: Fujian falls.
1927: Zhejiang falls.
1927: Shanghai and Nanjing fall: 'Bai Chongxi's forces entered Shanghai on 22 March 1927.
1927: Feng Yuxiang's Guominjun leaves its base in Shaanxi and takes Henan for the Nationalist side.
1928: the Nationalist army takes Jinan on 30 April.
1928: the Beiyang government ends in Beijing.
1928: Manchuria joins the Nationalist flag.
1928: the Beiyang Republic becomes the Nationalist Republic.
1930: Cliopatria's row returns to the Republic of China.
1930: the Guangxi clique, Feng Yuxiang and Yan Xishan keep their realms inside the Nationalist army, as at the end of the Northern Expedition (continued from the kuomintang dossier).
1930: Feng Yuxiang's Guominjun continues in Shaanxi and Henan.
1930: Yan Xishan's Shanxi clique continues in Shanxi, Beijing and Tianjin.
1930: Zhang Xueliang's Manchuria continues as a quasi-independent ally.
1930: the Communists hold the Jiangxi-Fujian border around Ruijin.
ledger.cpn: Chinese Communists (Jinggangshan and Jiangxi soviet bases)

ledger.x: 1930: the Central Plains War.
1930: the war breaks the arrangement with Yan Xishan, Feng Yuxiang and Li Zongren's Guangxi clique; Manchuria's Zhang Xueliang sides with Nanjing (not on the page).
1930: Feng Yuxiang's realm falls in the Central Plains War.
1930: Yan Xishan's realm falls in the Central Plains War.
May-June 1930: the Sino-Tibetan War opens.
1930: the vassalage ends with the khanate.
June 1930: Xinjiang's governor Jin Shuren abolishes the Kumul khanate and rules Hami as three ordinary districts, so the oasis passes from vassal to directly governed land.
1930: the Central Plains War ends.
1931: Japan invades Manchuria after the Mukden Incident.
1931: Zhang Xueliang's Manchuria ceases to be an ally when the Japanese overrun it; the page 'War was averted due to the Japanese invasion of Manchuria' (1931) does not say so itself.
1932: Manchukuo is proclaimed.
1932: the Japanese occupation of Manchuria ends in Manchukuo's proclamation (1 March 1932).
1933: the truces end the fighting.
1933: Rehe is annexed to Manchukuo.
12 November 1933: the Turkic Islamic Republic of Eastern Turkestan is proclaimed at Kashgar.
February 1934: Hui forces end the republic.
25 November 1935: the Japanese-backed East Hebei council declares itself independent.
1936: the Mongol military government is set up under Japanese patronage.
1937: Xinjiang passes under Soviet control.
1937: Beiping and Tianjin fall after the Marco Polo Bridge clash of 7 July.
1937: the capital goes to Wuhan.
1937: Nanjing falls in December.
1938: Japan holds North China.
1938: Kaifeng falls.
1938: the government re-establishes itself at Chongqing, 'the wartime seat of government until 1945'.
1938: Wuhan is abandoned.
October 1938: Japan takes the Guangdong coast.
1939: Japan invades Hainan.
1943: Xinjiang returns.
1944: Operation Ichi-Go.
September 1944: Ichi-Go enters Guangxi.
1944: the Three Districts rising founds the East Turkestan Republic.
ledger.cpn: East Turkestan Republic (Second East Turkestan Republic)

ledger.x: 1945: France returns Guangzhouwan.
1945: the Soviet Union enters Manchuria.
August 1945: Manchukuo ends and Rehe is Chinese again in law.
August 1945: Mengjiang ends and Inner Mongolia's Chahar and Suiyuan are Chinese again in law.
August 1945: Chinese Nationalist troops enter northern Vietnam to disarm the Japanese.
1945: Japan surrenders.
1945: the lower Yangtze is returned after the surrender of 2 September 1945.
1945: Wuhan and Anhui are returned after the surrender of 2 September 1945.
1945: Henan and Changsha are returned after the surrender of 2 September 1945.
1945: Japan 'formally surrendered on 2 September 1945' (Second Sino-Japanese War page); China 'regained' the lands lost since 1895.
1945: Japan 'formally surrendered on 2 September 1945' (Second Sino-Japanese War page); China 'regained' the lands lost since 1895.
1945: Japan 'formally surrendered on 2 September 1945' (Second Sino-Japanese War page); China 'regained' the lands lost since 1895.
1945: Japan 'formally surrendered on 2 September 1945' (Second Sino-Japanese War page); China 'regained' the lands lost since 1895.
1945: Japan 'formally surrendered on 2 September 1945' (Second Sino-Japanese War page); China 'regained' the lands lost since 1895.
September 1945: the Ili National Army reaches the Manas River.
ledger.cpn: East Turkestan Republic (Second East Turkestan Republic)

ledger.x: 1945: Taiwan returns to China.
1946: the Nationalists take over the cities of southern Manchuria as the Soviet army withdraws.
2 January 1946: the Preliminary Peace Agreement is signed at Dihua.
ledger.cpn: East Turkestan Republic (Second East Turkestan Republic)

ledger.x: 1946: the Soviets leave Manchuria.
1946: the war for the Northeast begins.
ledger.cpn: Communist Party of China (Chinese Soviet Republic, Shaan-Gan-Ning Border Region and Liberated Areas)

ledger.x: June 1946: the Chinese leave.
1947: the Nationalists take Yan'an.
ledger.cpn: Communist Party of China (Chinese Soviet Republic, Shaan-Gan-Ning Border Region and Liberated Areas)

ledger.x: 5 June 1947: Mongolian troops attack at Baitag Bogd.
Early July 1947: the Mongols return the land.
1948: the Liaoshen campaign ends the Manchurian war.
ledger.cpn: Communist Party of China (Chinese Soviet Republic, Shaan-Gan-Ning Border Region and Liberated Areas)

ledger.x: 1948: Manchuria is lost.
ledger.cpn: Communist Party of China (Chinese Soviet Republic, Shaan-Gan-Ning Border Region and Liberated Areas)

ledger.x: 1949: Beiping and Tianjin pass to the communists.
ledger.cpn: Communist Party of China (Chinese Soviet Republic, Shaan-Gan-Ning Border Region and Liberated Areas)

ledger.x: 1949: east-central China falls in the Huaihai campaign.
ledger.cpn: Communist Party of China (Chinese Soviet Republic, Shaan-Gan-Ning Border Region and Liberated Areas)

ledger.x: 1949: Nanjing falls on 23 April.
ledger.cpn: Communist Party of China (Chinese Soviet Republic, Shaan-Gan-Ning Border Region and Liberated Areas)

ledger.x: 1949: the government is at Guangzhou until 15 October.
1949: the People's Republic is proclaimed.
1949: the government moves to Chongqing, 15 October to 25 November, then Chengdu.
1949: Taipei becomes the capital.
1950: Hainan falls.
1950: Zhoushan falls.
February 1955: the Dachen Islands are evacuated and pass to the People's Republic.

wars.name: Zhili-Anhui War
wars.outcome: Zhili victory; 'After the 1920 Zhili-Anhui War, no taxes were remitted to Beijing other than Zhili province.'

wars.name: First Zhili-Fengtian War
wars.outcome: No border change is on the page.

wars.name: Second Zhili-Fengtian War
wars.outcome: No border change is on the page.

wars.name: Northern Expedition
wars.outcome: Nationalist victory: the Beiyang government ended on 6 June 1928; Manchuria followed on 29 December 1928.

wars.name: Central Plains War
wars.outcome: Chiang's victory, at the cost of bankruptcy.

wars.name: Sino-Tibetan War
wars.outcome: Chinese victory (infobox); separate truces in 1933 left the Upper Yangtze as the border.

wars.name: Japanese invasion of Manchuria
wars.outcome: Manchuria occupied from 18 September 1931; Manchukuo proclaimed 1 March 1932; Rehe annexed 4 March 1933.

wars.name: Second Sino-Japanese War
wars.outcome: Japanese surrender on 2 September 1945; Taiwan returned on 25 October 1945.

wars.name: Chinese Civil War
wars.outcome: Communist victory on the mainland: Manchuria (October-November 1948), Beiping (January 1949), Nanjing (23 April 1949), Chengdu (10 December 1949), Hainan (April 1950), Zhoushan (May 1950); the Republic retreated to Taiwan on 7 December 1949.

certainty.note: Warlord-era and war-time fronts, the Tibetan, Outer Mongolian and Xinjiang frontiers and the occupation lines are approximate; Manchukuo's and Rehe's boundaries and the coast are firm.
Taiwan, Penghu, Kinmen and Matsu: island coasts; Hainan and Zhoushan are firm in 1950.
